summary: The feature describes how local gyms and fitness enthusiasts are adopting eco-friendly fitness practices, from sustainable gym design and green outdoor programs to biodegradable equipment, local plant-based nutrition, and gear recycling. It cites a study showing a 75% rise in popularity of green workout options in 2023 and profiles people and initiatives driving the trend. It also notes mental health benefits and frames the movement as a model for other industries.
one_line: Local gyms and fitness communities are embracing sustainability through green gym design, outdoor programs, eco-friendly equipment, mindful nutrition, and recycling initiatives.
key_facts: A study by the Local Fitness Trends Institute, headed by Dr. Cassie Tran, found eco-friendly workout options have seen a 75% increase in popularity since the beginning of the year.
EcoFit Hub, a local fitness center, opened on October 3, 2023, built with recycled materials, energy-efficient lighting and water-saving fixtures.
EcoFit Hub founder Mike Jennings says its cardio machines run on renewable energy, its weight equipment is made from recycled metals, and it provides reusable water bottles.
Fitness trainer Holly Sanders launched the 'Fit for the Future' program on September 20, 2023, combining exercise routines with tree-planting and community clean-ups.
A 'Run for the Reefs' event is planned for November 12, 2023, organized by a coalition of gyms and conservationists to raise funds for coral reef restoration projects.
Inventor Daniel Choi launched a line of biodegradable yoga mats on September 1, 2023, made from natural rubber and jute fibers.
Smart technology is being built into workout equipment that generates power as people exercise.
Registered Dietitian Emily Patel advises clients to source food locally and favor plant-based diets, citing lower transport emissions and a lower carbon footprint.

Laura Shen, entrepreneur and environmentalist, initiated the 'Gear for Good' campaign on September 9, 2023, in which donated used sports equipment is refurbished and given to underprivileged communities.
Many gyms have started recycling programs for old sneakers and workout gear, and some businesses upcycle the materials into new gym equipment.
Psychologist Dr. Robert Lee says green workouts help reduce stress and anxiety and give individuals a profound sense of purpose.
Gyms are partnering with environmental organizations to host 'fitness fundraisers' and are offering organic, locally-sourced snacks and beverages.
